newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends higher, deal thin.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends higher, deal thin.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher after a quiet trading day, with buying interest again absent, dealers said.
Dealing was sluggish with most buyers still keeping at the sidelines, waiting for attractive prices, they said.
"There were some enquiries from Far-east and European buyers," a dealer said, adding that some buyers are covering for their year-end buying programes.
"Some buyers were seen looking for SMR grades and RSS 1 sheet but there weren't much business transacted," the dealer added.
A higher Tokyo market also boosted prices slightly up at the close, dealer said.
December RSS Ones buyer ended half a cent up at 320 cents ($1.26) a kg and December SMR 20 buyer was up a cent to 3098.
Traders said SMR CV was offered at 364 cents, SMR L at 344 cents and SMR 5 at 319 cents.
The INRO five-day average was 244.34 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Nov 22 from 244.39 on Nov 21. The daily indicator was 243.63 against 244.43.
